title: Solid, Liquid & Gas
description: Grade 2 Science: solids, liquids and gases. What matter is, the three states, and how water changes between ice, water and steam — with an interactive states-of-matter simulation.

topics.title: Everything Is Matter
topics.concept:
Everything around us is made of matter. Anything that takes up space and can be felt is matter.

Matter comes in three forms, called states of matter:

  • 🧊 Solids — like a rock or a book.
  • 💧 Liquids — like water or milk.
  • 💨 Gases — like the air around us.

recap: Everything around us is made of matter.
Matter takes up space and can be felt.
The three states of matter are solid, liquid and gas.

wonder.text: Your chair, your juice and the air in a balloon are all different. Yet they have one big thing in common. What is it?

qa.q: Is air really matter? I can't see it!
qa.a: Yes! Air is a gas, and it is matter. You cannot see it, but you can feel it as wind, and it fills up a balloon. So it takes up space — that makes it matter.
Almost everything you can touch — solids, liquids and gases — is matter. Light and sound are special; they are not matter, but nearly everything else is!

topics.title: Solids
topics.concept:
A solid has its own shape and size that do not change on their own.

  • 🪨 A rock, 📕 a book, 🥄 a spoon, 🪑 a chair are all solids.
  • You can hold a solid in your hand.
  • A solid keeps its shape, even if you move it to a different place.

If you put a ball in a box, the ball still stays a ball — it keeps its shape.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="150" fill="#eef6ff"/><text x="55" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🪨</text><text x="55" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Rock</text><text x="165" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">📕</text><text x="165" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Book</text><text x="275" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🥄</text><text x="275" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Spoon</text><text x="165" y="138" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Solids keep their shape</text></svg>
recap: A solid keeps its own shape and size.
Rocks, books, spoons and chairs are solids.
A solid does not change shape on its own.

wonder.text: Why does a book keep its shape, but water does not?

qa.q: Is sand a solid? It pours like a liquid!
qa.a: Sand IS a solid! It is just made of millions of tiny solid grains. Each grain keeps its own shape — together they can pour, but every grain is solid.

qa.q: Can a solid change its shape?
qa.a: A solid keeps its shape on its own. It only changes if we cut it, break it or squash it — like clay we press with our hands.

topics.title: Liquids
topics.concept:
A liquid can flow and pour. It does not have its own shape — it takes the shape of whatever holds it.

  • 💧 Water, 🥛 milk, 🧃 juice and 🛢️ oil are liquids.
  • Pour a liquid into a round glass and it becomes round.
  • Pour the same liquid into a tall bottle and it becomes tall!
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="150" fill="#eef9ff"/><text x="55" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">💧</text><text x="55" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Water</text><text x="165" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🥛</text><text x="165" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Milk</text><text x="275" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🧃</text><text x="275" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Juice</text><text x="165" y="138" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Liquids flow and pour</text></svg>
recap: A liquid takes the shape of its container.
Water, milk, juice and oil are liquids.

wonder.text: Pour juice into a cup, then a bottle. It changes shape each time! How?

qa.q: Why does spilt water spread out?
qa.a: A liquid has no shape of its own, so when it spills it just flows and spreads to fill the flat space. That is why we mop up spills quickly!

qa.q: Does the amount of liquid change when I pour it?
qa.a: No — only the SHAPE changes, not the amount. One cup of water poured into a bottle is still one cup of water.

topics.title: Gases
topics.concept:
A gas has no shape of its own and spreads out to fill all the space it can. Most gases are invisible.

  • 💨 The air around us is a mix of gases.
  • 🎈 Gas fills up a balloon and makes it bigger.
  • ☁️ Steam from hot tea is water in gas form.

We cannot usually see gases, but we can feel moving air as wind, and we breathe a gas called oxygen to stay alive.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="150" fill="#f3f0ff"/><text x="55" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">💨</text><text x="55" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Air</text><text x="165" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🎈</text><text x="165" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Balloon</text><text x="275" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">☁️</text><text x="275" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Steam</text><text x="165" y="138" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Gases spread out</text></svg>
recap: A gas has no shape and spreads to fill all the space.
Air is a gas all around us; we cannot usually see it.
Steam from hot water is a gas.

wonder.text: When you blow up a balloon, what fills it? You cannot even see it!

qa.q: If I can't see air, how do I know it is there?
qa.a: You feel it! Wave your hand and you feel air move. A balloon fills with it, and the wind that flies a kite is moving air. Air is a real gas all around us.

qa.q: Is the steam from hot tea a gas?
qa.a: Yes! When water gets very hot, it turns into a gas called water vapour, or steam. That misty cloud above hot tea is water in its gas form.

topics.title: Water Can Change!
topics.concept:
Water is special — it can be a solid, a liquid AND a gas! It changes when it gets hotter or colder:

  • ❄️ Very cold water freezes into ice (a solid).
  • ☀️ Ice warms up and melts back into water (a liquid).
  • 🔥 Very hot water boils into steam (a gas).

So the same water can be ice in the freezer, water in your glass, and steam above hot tea!
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 135" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="320" height="135" fill="#eef6ff"/><defs><marker id="ch" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#3CA7FF"/></marker></defs><text x="53.333333333333336" y="72" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🧊</text><text x="53.333333333333336" y="108" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Ice</text><line x1="75.33333333333334" y1="62" x2="138" y2="62" stroke="#3CA7FF" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ch)"/><text x="160" y="72" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">💧</text><text x="160" y="108" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Water</text><line x1="182" y1="62" x2="244.66666666666669" y2="62" stroke="#3CA7FF" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ch)"/><text x="266.6666666666667" y="72" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">☁️</text><text x="266.6666666666667" y="108" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Steam</text><text x="160" y="128" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#16a06a" text-anchor="middle">Water can change!</text></svg>
recap: Water can be a solid (ice), a liquid (water) or a gas (steam).
Cold freezes water into ice; heat melts ice and boils water into steam.
The same water changes state when it gets hotter or colder.

wonder.text: Ice, water and steam look so different — but they are all the same thing. How?

qa.a: Heat! When ice gets warmer — out of the freezer, in your hand or in the sun — it melts and turns back into liquid water.

qa.q: Where does a puddle go on a sunny day?
qa.a: The Sun's heat slowly turns the puddle water into an invisible gas (water vapour) that floats up into the air. This is called evaporation.

questions.q: Everything around us is made of…
questions.explanation: Everything that takes up space and can be felt is matter.
Milk flows and takes the shape of its cup — it is a liquid.
A solid keeps its own shape and size.

questions.q: The air around us is a…
questions.explanation: Air is a gas — it has no shape and fills the space around us.

questions.q: Water becomes ICE when it is very…
questions.explanation: Very cold water freezes into solid ice.

questions.q: Steam from hot tea is water in the form of a…
questions.explanation: Hot water turns into steam, which is a gas.

questions.q: Why does juice change shape when poured into different cups?
options: Liquids take the shape of their container
questions.explanation: A liquid has no shape of its own, so it takes the shape of whatever holds it.

questions.q: Sand can pour, but it is a solid because…
options: It is made of tiny solid grains that keep their shape
questions.explanation: Sand is millions of tiny solid grains; each keeps its own shape.

questions.q: Put in order from COLDEST to hottest: water, steam, ice.
Where does a puddle go on a sunny day?
options: The Sun turns it into gas that floats into the air
questions.explanation: The Sun's heat turns the water into an invisible gas — this is evaporation.

options: The same water in three different states
questions.explanation: They are all the same water — just in solid, liquid and gas states.
